title: The Object Before the Answer
surface:
A leaves the room while I choose an object and B remembers it. When A returns, B asks a series of questions. In three rounds the lists are:
“Cup? Piano? Keys?”
“Spoon? Vase? Iceberg? Watch?”
“Chair? Plate? Cup? Bed? Coin?”
A says yes only to the last item each time, always correctly. The everyday objects are present, but there is no piano, iceberg or bed. A neither sees nor overhears my choices. How does the trick work?
solution: A and B have agreed on a verbal marker: an object that is absent from the room. B asks about some present objects, then names an absent one, then immediately names the chosen target. Piano, iceberg and bed are the markers; keys, watch and coin follow them. A recognizes the signal rather than reading anyone’s mind.

facts.text: They have agreed to use an absent object as a verbal marker.
The item immediately after that marker is the chosen object and receives the yes answer.
There is no eavesdropping, electronic communication or signal based on tone, color or gestures.

unknowns: Their identities and other furnishings are unspecified; piano, iceberg and bed are definitely absent.
hints: Compare the item immediately before each correct answer.
Are those three preceding objects actually in the room?
Naming an absent object signals that the next item is the target.
